I’ve been saying it since the announcement that they were cutting service. Imagine this with me. Bungie spends the next few months completely Silent after the announcement.. the community reacts, they are upset. They are frustrated at the lost potential and we all play the hell out of Destiny 2. Then next year at E3 there’s a new trailer announcement for an unknown game. The screens black . Cut to Cayde talking about how we shouldn’t go gently into the night. That we should rage, rage rage against the dying of the light. Cut to text on the screen that says “we heard you” and then in big text we see “Destiny 3” they spend 4 to 5 years of the development. They take every amazing part of the first and second game and build it all on a new engine. I think I can speak for all of us and say that every single one of us would return and play the new game and the community would absolutely lose their minds with excitement. New players would also come in droves .They have the potential to create the biggest heart string pulling announcement in gaming history.

The game needs a full reset. Since D1 original writers left (during that game’s cycle), the new guys and girls have been replacing the original story with their take, and taking characters in weird paths. Often I had the impression that they changed things only to leave their mark, since most of the changes made no sense.

As a main titan, I would like to say that i rathered much how did Hallowfire Heart worked in the way it did before this last update, this is because now the energy regeneration feels too restrictive in general but very severe when you still not getting the super to activate the exotic's armour perk, this is even worse if you consider that the exotic Ashen Wake gets overshadowed by Hallowfire Heart because of this last not that good "buff" in general, this feels sad considering that many other titan exotics, or even other exotics from other classes give better energy regeneration. Another case are the "An insurmountable skull" the "Armamentarium" and "Hoarfrost Z" exotics, they are good but definetly they could get a better buff in this last endgame sand box era meta, so these are just a few examples of armour exotics that still need a buff for it to have a better quality end game usage. Another examples would be weapons such as sunshot, it's buff was not really the "catalyst buff" anyone or just me expected to get (still lacks damage) neither the one many guns deserved, they deserved a bit better and for the seasonal artifact mods, bungie or whoever is making these changes they do always do the same, they do not bring back the artifact mods everyone loved and needed for certain exotics to work like "Defibrillating arc mod" (because arc subclass does have a poor and mediocre heallth regeneration or even none at all), so if they are not willing to bring back those mods, the least they can do it's for them to try to integrate those last mods in some way or another inside the game like "subclass buffs" or in other way. They do still need to give us some really good buffs instead of nerfs, and my argument on this it's because instead of a limited and restricted meta, we do need infact to be able to use a huge amount of USEFULL variety of playstyles for us to actually enjoy and stay in this game's finale update. My first time playing Destiny 1 was on my original D1 PS4 and right after I PCS'd (Permanent Change of Duty Station) to Germany. I couldn't have been more than 23, and I only knew maybe 3 or 4 guys from the flight that I was assigned to at the time, so it was pretty isolating living off base initially. My buddy and I knew Destiny was coming out, and I was waiting for my Destiny PS4 bundle to come in. By the time I joined him, he was a Titan main, probably lvl 10 or so already, and I was trying out a Hunter for the first time, exploring the Cosmodrone as he showed me the ropes. Maaan, when I tell you that even though he and I had just gotten off a 12-hour shift, that I was hooked from the moment I was brought to life by my ghost, that we played like 5 hours straight that night alone.. What a time in gaming, and just a truly unique experience. As you and Byf said, Destiny became our third home, and we invested so much time and effort into everything we did that I can't imagine how my friendships, some that I still have today, would have lasted without having something like Destiny to help bridge all those years that I was overseas and still playing with my friends online. It felt like hanging with the boys for us, with objectives, helping each other get new gear, absolutely destroying teams in Cruicble because some played more tactfully in mind, and we worked well in squads, you name it man. Just no other game like it or time in gaming in general like the time playing Destiny with so many people. I too got invested into Destiny more by hearing all the lore videos Byf, Evaze, Dankhe, and so many others have made over the years. I remember when Destiny brought Datto in for the first time, and that blew my mind to see someone I watched on YouTube actually be in the house, tryign t obe voice for player demands with something we all grew to love. I could go on and on for hours about Destiny and what it means to me at this point, so I'll stop my comment here, but you get the point.

The feeling of hopping randomly onto Cross’ stream to watch while eating after playing hours of the update and seeing something I have never seen before, coupled with dialogue from Bael that I knew I hadn’t heard, made me crazy.
I went through all the possibilities “is it Equilibrium because I hadn’t played that?” Well, nothing I’d seen of the dungeon had actual Bael dialogue, I don’t think, and I’ve seen plenty of the dungeon, and then I saw the red architecture of shadow keep, and I thought “is it a new mission? A small little thing?” And then the previously hidden mission icon on the left of the screen popped up when the objective updated, and I saw the exotic mission icon with a name I’d never seen before and suddenly went to myself “there’s an exotic mission?”

I checked reddit and discord after and people knew about it there, so I guess I managed to luck out and miss all of that until rejoining his stream. It’s a magic like really no other in Destiny learning there’s a secret like that, and it’s always amazing.

I’m going to miss updates to this game. Reading all the lore tabs makes me think of what could have been, and what was going to be. Funnily enough, there was a Pantheon armour lore tab talking about literally about “what could have been”.

Given the teaser at the end of Renegades and the entire suite of DEO weapons and a whole DEO lore tab, we were absolutely going to go to DEO headquarters, in old Chicago, finally. And considering how good the content is when they release some, I can’t help but think that it was going to be amazing. Imagine all the weird, anomalous exotics we’d find, maybe all things the DEO was investigating. I love when exotics (like the new hand cannon) have a story where they were found or used by another before you. Bungie didn’t do that enough honestly, and it’s great. Imagine the raid we would’ve gotten. Some trippy, governmental organization shit in a swamp.

27:21 on the ogre boss, you can fight him without entering into the no-spawn mode, by going to get a different worm I found high up on a wall, up and to the far left corner of the room if facing looking out from the center arm extending out from the boss room. Way up there is a free worm that requires no dunking, and you can get up to it without even triggering the boss, and you can go hit the crystal with the worm without even triggering the darkness zone. There is also a cheese spot for the ogre boss here, around the back of the boss room where you later shoot the symbols; you can hop up and shoot the ogre with primary thru the windows, if you have lion rampants or the warlock wings exotics that let you hover and shoot; not sure how it well it would work with hunter.

Bungi and Sony, a marriage made in Hell. They have been working so hard to end D2. I just got on for about 5 minutes, and down went their servers. I was one of the first people invited to play D1. I was friends with one of the software developers back then. We wrote two games and sold them to Atari. Bungi had one heck of a team and was going places. Sony stepped in years later and bought them out. Sony is a good company; they are very good with technology, but they also enjoy making money. They have killed D2, and many on here keep asking for D3, let me clue you all in: it is not going to happen. Enjoy the ride for as long as it lasts, keep track of the number playing, and when it hits bottom, the switch will be turned off.

Going to start out by saying that this idea is beyond a ‘Hail Mary’ but, never the less, could provide some hope(cope).  

Maybe we’re praying to(trying to appease) the wrong gods, maybe, instead of trying to appeal to Sony, we should be pleading to Microsoft… I know, it sounds crazy, but let us not forget that Xbox is on the back leg and really only maintains, in large part, due to Microsoft’s ‘infinite money’ cheat.   

When was the last time Xbox was a juggernaut in the gaming industry?… The answer is, when Halo was the biggest game in the world. What else did Microsoft(Xbox) have at that time, Bungie. I know the Microsoft-Bungie bridge was burned a long time ago, but could you imagine the homecoming!?!  What better way to get your console back on top than to bring Destiny, Bungie, and all their property back to Microsoft. 

At its peak Destiny is the best fps looter shooter on the market and has been for over a decade, at its full potential it’s one of the biggest IP’s and games in the world, and I don’t think Destiny, as a franchise, has reached its full potential yet. What does Xbox need to get back on top?  Some secret sauce; D3 could be that secret sauce. 

What if Microsoft opened up that ‘Scrooge McDuck-esque’ vault and purchased Bungie and their properties from Sony…? What if Microsoft then went out and hired back as many of the old guard from years past at Bungie as possible…? What if Microsoft/Xbox merged Bungie with Halo studios(formerly 343 industries, formerly the portion of Bungie that decided to stay behind at Microsoft when Bungie and Microsoft split)…? Not only could a Destiny 3 be getting made, but do we think all that combined talent could ‘right the ship’ for Halo?  And what if Microsoft went full cheat code, turned on the infinite money and resources cheats and delivered, not only, a banger and return to form for the Halo franchise(and a console exclusive), but also a Destiny 3 just in time for the next-gen Xbox release, do we think that Microsoft could get Xbox back on top with that? I don’t know, but I can cope.  Fight forever Guardians!!

Still probably my favorite expansion. The area/story, Stasis, raid and Europa was great and the seasons after were amazing. Sunsetting sadly corroded everything about Destiny though but that didn’t stop me from enjoying it

37:40 Stasis had a better introduction than Strand by far. Wielding darkness was a big deal back then, and it was specifically given to us by The Witness. Finding Strand was pure luck and it had little lore implications. It was just a macguffin to get to the Veil. It also came out of nothing. Stasis was hinted at the end of Shadowkeep, when Eris interacted with the Statue. Strand felt like a new toy Bungie thought would be fun.
Thats when I started during beyond light. Really had me hooked!

To me, Beyond Light was when the game’s Darkness arc truly began. 
The pause screen was darker. All the mods were streamlined for newer mods. The music even became darker and more ominous. 

It was also during a dark time that the pandemic was in full effect. Good times
6:07 THE DYNAMIC WEATHER SYSTEM 🗣️❄️

Beyond Light has some of the best environmental and non verbal storytelling of any video game I think I’ve ever played. Clovis Bray’s malignant influence is all over this expansion and I love the detail of “New Riis” being haphazardly placed on top of the old city.

Beyond Light was the real turning point for me that kept me really hooked beyond the initial missions. The OST and the lore especially. And how the raid told a story. That's how I met my forever clan.

I also somehow got my irl friends into the game around this time. The late nights of Gambit are still really strong memories.

I will always stand by my opinion that had sunsetting not happened, Beyond Light and the year of seasons that followed would be remembered as by far and away the best year Destiny ever had. The level of immersion and intrigue they brought forth in their storytelling this year felt so special, and it felt as though every turned corner made me more infatuated with the game. 

This year gave us an 'ice' subclass, (my wife) Eramis and her House of Salvation, (my wife) Elsie finally having the time to explain, the beauty of Europa and the frozen Bray Labs, the Deep Stone Crypt with Morning Star space station, Crow's return and journey alongside Glint in finding himself, the Eliksni at home again below the Traveller with the House of Light lead by Mithrax, an introduction and challenge by the Empress of the Cabal with Caiatl, as well as the long awaited reconnection with Mara and her plan for the dangers ahead. 

If only the vast gameplay improvements to subclasses/associated verb usage and the campaign structure/difficulty that were built up in the past couple of years could've been there for it all </3

This allows them to do what they did to the red war and forsaken campaigns. They can remove delete or even take it away for no reason and there’s nothing you can do about it bc you agreed to it in the user agreements. Something that can’t be done if you owned the physical copy. Which is also why they stopped making the physical version like 2 years after it came out. You don’t see crap like this with steam, but they certainly could if they wanted to. It’s a shame….

4:22 I remember getting my friends on multiple nights a week for raids a while back, and it was the dream. They all were kind of new to D2, and I was the only veteran player. I had done my fair share of raiding with LFG teams over the years, but raiding felt like a lofty goal for a team where only one guy had experience. 

I sat in a call one night with a full fireteam of six. All of us happened to get on coincidentally, and then one of us went "We should do a raid lmao." and then we decided you know what, sure. I guided 5 new light guardians through their first raid experience. Better yet, they wanted to do GoS  just for extra laughs. It was the raid I'd done the least, but I explained every encounter to them all. We wiped countless times, but after we got the slightest mechanical progress in the first encounter, they were all hooked. No one was angry if someone caused a wipe. We all understood the situation, and were determined to beat it as a team. 

The sanctified mind died that night right as the sun rose. No one ever thought to sleep. Determination overrode exhaustion for all of us. 

We would go on to do every raid we could, farming each one for the exotics and best rolls for weapons we wouldn't even use, just as an excuse to do them. 

That fire burned so bright and was so fun for us all, but it slowly died and no one got on anymore. 

Now I'm back to being a solo player, and it sucks a lot. LFGs being in a barren state now makes raiding basically impossible for me now. It's strange hearing such an eerily similar communal story

Denial:

Anger:

Bargaining:
With the state of play coming up and all the push to make the emotes and whatnot, this was a chance to let our voice be heard. Although I am stretching the narrative here a little bit, this is where this stage lands. 
Depression:
Afterwards and after all the VA’s came out and talked about their feelings, both in and out of character, reality hits and it’s sad that the fate saga ends here.
Acceptance:

PlayStation’s entire legacy is built on dominant, prestige single-player experiences. Right now, players are completely fatigued by live-service games and loot boxes. Showcasing games like these two at a massive event would have driven home the point that Sony is still the undisputed king of premium, single-player action-RPGs.

Both of these titles look absolutely stunning and bring incredibly fresh gameplay mechanics to the table—from Nezha’s flowing, celestial aerial-and-ground combat to Jinyiwei’s insane Wuxia martial arts and unique sandbox deduction mechanics. Sony needs to put these games front and center at the next showcase. They represent the exact kind of deep lore, high-octane action, and creative passion that the PlayStation community actually wants to support.

We absolutely thought the whole community would come together to Boycott this regardless of the excuses, and they did for a little while but Bungie kept plugging away and super hardcore people, people with no other outlets, and even content creators never left but rather just dealt with it. (like a red headed stepchildren, as the saying goes) As the content kept rolling out in expedited fashion and little by little more people kept coming back over time. 

Yeah, sure, during this time everyone was struggling. The community loved this game so much it litterally ripped everything apart and it has been a patchwork of fixes from both sides of the fence to keep this frankenstein alive,  point blank. The player counts during the more recent time frames, that bore any resemblances to that of very early/ Forsaken timeframe players counts had been, were basicly the real and I mean the real hardcore fans that were excited about end game content or just plain capitulated back in because they may have thought or felt that this was it "might as well because it's over now".

Here's the thing though there still are those of us, how ever many we may be, still sitting on the sidelines. We all still would love to come back pick up where we left off grinding out that whisper of the worm or outbreak prime catalyst that was almost completed the night of the sunset, but haven't because we took the long road in hopes of coming back to a game that left us behind. In a perfect world. All of us player count wise would repopulate those servers just like the good ole days if they could figure out how to rewind the hands of time, but we don't live in a perfect world now do we.

The only solution to not having a time machine is, remastering Destiny into a 3rd iteration for what I call a D3i. If done right everyone still waiting to come back can eventually come back to a complete story line play through so that we all are caught up on the same page as those of your who stayed til the bitter end. I must add, While shilling out alot of money and time for the product you lived through these past 6 years. (continuing) While simultaneously providing the ground work for moving forward in the story line with new content releases on a slightly longer time frame schedule. "NO CONTENT TO BE VAULTED EVER AGAIN"  To me this is the only level way to equalize the player base and the the budgetary means and needs for the company going forward.

Ignoring the removed raids and the recent raid and dungeon with Tiered gear, that’s 10 dungeons, 9 raids, each with their own armour set being reprised and given two set bonuses each, for a total of 19 sets and 38 total bonus perks. Goddamn.

In addition, there’s the updated tiered weapons from each raid, most of which seem to have refreshed loot pools (although the degree of that for more recent RAD weapons remains to be seen), and possibly new origin traits, even if they had ones already, maybe.

And all that is ignoring the Black Armoury weapons they’re reprising, in addition to the implied reprises of at least some of Leviathan, Eater of Worlds, and Crown of Sorrow weapons. (I’m not sure if their armour sets will return, and also the splash art of Pantheon 2.0 in the original announcement post only includes the bosses of those raids, but I assume that Scourge of the Past and Spire of Stars bosses will be included as well)

It’s all shaping up to be a whole lot of stuff to do, stuff to watch, and stuff in general, and I only mentioned the Pantheon rewards. It’ll be fun to see people collecting all of what they’re adding. Well done, dev team, for this one last hurrah.

Okay, hear me out for your Void Titan Sentinel Shield Super for support purposes. I’ve had this idea for a while now:

So when Sentinel Shield is deployed (the actual shield), bullets fired through it from the player’s side increase in damage. What if there was a progress bar tied into the Sentinel Shield mechanic? As weapons are fired through the shield, the bar fills. When the Suped Titan activates Shield Throw, the damage/stagger output and number of ricochets of the shield scales with how full the bar was at the time of activation. What this does is allows the Suped Titan to output more damage, gives the other fireteam members more incentive to group alongside the Titan, AND gives enemies a chance to damage the team during Shield Throws so it’s not a 1-sided OP Super. Risk vs Reward. “Do I throw my shield to damage, or should I keep it up longer until the team takes out more enemies?” It gives the player a strategic ultimatum, and not just has them keeping a shield up the whole super.

Along with this, I would have the Super length extend depending on how many times the Shield Throw RICOCHETS off targets, rather than how much damage is blocked with Sentinel Shield. This also plays into the Risk vs Reward ultimatum. “Do I need to throw my shield to add a little more time to cover my teammates? Or should I keep it up longer to allow them to recover?”

I think this would play a lot better into the TANK build for Sentinel Shield, and encourage more team communication and coordination amongst the fireteam. But that’s just me LOL

For those who havent played GTA Online: its an open world where dozens of players can be running around in at once. you start off with no money, no cars, no properties, no gears (weapons, grenades) but there are many ways of making money (usually crimes). You start slow with some gun-4-hire work, you may do missions where you protect someone, or youre tasked with taking out a group of drug dealers. There is more lucrative missions like the famous HEISTS, which will have you run a few setup/prep missions with a group that end in a big execution where you steal something worth a lot of money. You may spend the money getting better guns and cars that will hopefully help you in missions (more money) . After you save up a big chunk of money, you can buy your own company building where you run your own operations and have opportunities for big money. maybe you buy a dock that unlocks missions where you can steal large merchandise and store there for large sales. more money, more cars, more properties, better money making opportunities.

Marathon was obviously meant to be a side game. A medium sized project that may attract some destiny players, but is meant to attract those who are not destiny players already. Something that had decent potential, but wouldn’t detract from Destiny 2. In a big way. I’m sure many knew that an extraction shooter is a niche genre and doesn’t have the growth potential to be the next big thing. But with all the bad decisions of bungie management leading to layoffs. This turned a side project into their hail Mary. a $40 PVP only game was never meant to take more resources than all of destiny. But they needed it to succeed after final shape didn’t make enough and they couldn’t make edge of fate stick the landing. They needed to give hope to Sony. so it makes sense to ask why did we lose destiny for marathon. We weren’t meant to, but poor business decisions made it necessary. If destiny hadn’t already been in a below target revenue state, marathon could have simply been a side game. Also, it’s clear how horribly inefficient bungees development process is. Apparently it takes dozens of devs just to keep the game on not even making anything new. I get game development is hard, but much smaller studios with much smaller funding are making things that blow away What bungee has been putting out recently. In a vacuum marathon is a good game but I am sure another developer could’ve made it for a fifth the price.

Now when I come back and look at the portal I don't see any point in doing anything, it feels like loving someone and spending your entire life with them but gradually over time they become a completely different person from who you fell in love with.  I still love Destiny 2 and I would like for it to go back to what it was, but deep down I know that's not going to happen.

It is valid to pay money for experiences rather than things you own forever, like a cruise or a vacation, but games are sold on an expectation of long-term access. The way people say, "Don't worry what'll happen in a week or a month or a year bro, enjoy the now!" comes off as less sincere and more corporate apologia, especially when they don't recognize the context that this is exactly how corporations want you to think. It also starts feeling like a sneaky appeal to FOMO: "Try it before it's gone!" I'm not saying that it is shilling, but it's exactly what shills would say in substance, and so no matter how sincere it actually is, that makes it suspect to me.

This is what’s wrong with Extraction Shooters, there is no rest of the game. The premise of The Dark Zone in The Division was you go there with a higher chance of finding loot that if you could extract it, the benefit is you can use that item in the rest of the game, but you might have to fight like hell to get it. Now in these, there is no rest of the game. So you fight to get an item, just to be placed in a position where your going to lose the item in a inventory wipe or a match, but why keep it anyway when there is nowhere to use it. So essentially, these are poor extraction shooters because you’re all fighting to get something that you have to lose anyway, there is no actual payoff. You just fused death match, with extraction with BR but not real payoff. This mode isn’t meant to be by itself and when it is, it’s really just a different take on deathmatch. I think the game that will be the most successful will need to use it as it was intended like The Division, because the majority people are looking at these games like Looter Shooters, but imagine playing Destiny or Borderlands and never being able to keep the loot you fight so hard to get. That’s my two cents

Rise of Iron is remembered so fondly because of the cool af story, the gear, the general life updates, pvp, the amount of content outside of mainline content, the communication and transparency from Bungie and the raid.
I’m not saying that it did everything great, but it gave us a bit of everything and did it very well. Accompanied by the April, Dawning and Age of Triumph updates and the lead up events to the DLC drop, it’s 100% one of the best times a lot of players had in Destiny’s lifetime.
Bungie straight up told us that it would be the last DLC before D2 which definitely helped with the hype and enjoyment.
The box game content model, while it definitely sucked during those drought periods, I think it’s better than the drip feed model we have now.
Massive content updates that would completely change the game, the feeling of excitement knowing it would drop (mostly) on time and the amazing trailers leading up to it.
We’d receive more than one exotic and loads more weapons per content drop which changes every way we played.

D2’s content model of drip feed gives the feeling of constant satisfaction, but at a lesser feeling, but also the feeling of something missing. Each season drops content and a lesser number of weapons and gear compared to the box sale model of DLC drop that would completely change up the lootpool from greens all the way to exotics. D2 ditches content after a season ends, including weapons and armor without a proper replacement like D1 DLCs. This 100% leads to burnout on the dev’s end. Why would I care about my work if it’ll be removed in 3-4 months?
The same idea we have about our gear snd sunsetting absolutely applies to the devs, even if they don’t say it, but you can most definitely see it at times.
My rant is done. Thx for coming to my TED Talk.

Jolder is mentioned to be the "Champion" of the Iron Lords against a few Warlords in D1/D2 lore, and in D: Rising, she's their main "Champion"; a title that meant she was their go-to representative of the Iron Lords' might if ever someone needed to be 1v1'd.

Efrideet may have stood a chance at claiming the title, but she was the youngest of the Iron Lords, and probably came into their ranks later into their existence (admittedly my own conjecture), and Jolder (in D: Rising) expresses how she doesn't think there's even a need for a "Champion" anymore (while the Iron Lords were still very much active). It may just be that Efrideet didn't care to be "Champion", or that it was simply not a role anymore by the time she joined (D: Rising), or that it was never an official role (D1/D2), in which case we actually have no hard indication on which Iron Lord was actually "strongest".

Radegast (while no doubt powerful) was never really revered in the lore **FOR** his strength-- but more that everyone rallied behind him because he was an immensely charismatic and optimistic person that believed in everyone, saw the best in them, and made them stronger through the powers of friendship (anime protagonist style).

Felwinter is mentioned as being a ruthless and underhanded combatant that ended a few warlords, but he was a warlord himself, and the Iron Lords hunted him down. Inevitably, he joined the Iron Lords, and they let him fight Shaxx-- who then proceeded to be a Dark Souls boss that repeated sent Felwinter back to the bonfire, and was NEVER beaten by Felwinter. While this may speak more to how powerful Shaxx is, rather than how weak Felwinter is; much of the lore on Felwinter is just him aura-farming while actually taking "L"s the whole time, lol.

It's important to note, however: simply being the best/strongest 1v1 combatant is a rather "in a vacuum" question/answer. It assumes a lot of variables: favorable match-up, an honorable duel with no tricks/breaking of rules, it's not a fight involving a team/squad/army, it's not a prolonged war of logistics (attrition or morale), it's not a battle of wits or subterfuge, it's not a battle for any objective other than a simple death match, etc.

I believe that one of the reasons D1 was better imo, is the 70 aspect ratio. But it was special at the time, also it felt like the developers had a great time creating something new. D2 seemed old before it really got started. There’s something to say about the birth of a new type of game, but I feel the overall story was really interesting and engaging.

The quality of tone, writing, and overall direction is night and day when it comes to D1 and D2. You can obviously tell that VA’s like Morla and Nolan were given direction to give a darker vibe and it really did fit Destiny so much better than whatever is they’re doing even today. 

Another thing is that we never felt like the main character in Destiny 1 and that was a good thing. We felt like we were just a small part of a much larger universe and unfortunately that changed immediately in Destiny 2. We went from foot soldier for good to main character and honestly that killed the scope and overall feeling of once again being part of a larger world. 

Tbh Instead of keeping the “guardian” a character that is just doing their best and our best barely being good enough, we became the absolute fucking boss. It came across even in the difficulty of the game. The game has gotten much easier from an overall basic player vs enemy perspective.  I think they really fucked up by allowing the guardians to just obliterate almost anything. There should be some enemies that no matter what we just aren’t gonna be able to handle without several minutes of chipping away. Once again this would help with scope. 

I really do Bungie made just a huge mistake lightening the tone and mood of Destiny when it got to D2. The overall tone and direction was WAY TOO light and humorous. It was not a good choice imho. I think it served as a detriment to where the game was going. It didn’t kill the franchise obviously, but it normalized the struggle between good vs evil too much, so that nothing since has felt as high stakes as it did in Destiny 1. Just my 2 cents. 

TLDR; Bungie fucked up by giving our guardian main character energy, and also fucked up by trivializing good vs evil (see the shitty, campy and writing of D2 year one)

For some extra context, Black Desert (the mmo) is named after the magical "black stones" that were found in the Valencia Desert in the game's history, where alot of people  went to war over said black stones because ooh shiny magic rock.
It's called the "Black" desert to the people *not* from the desert due to its abundance of black stones, but known as the "Red" desert by people who live in the desert due to all the blood that was shed during those wars over the black stones. 
Crimson desert's world has a pretty large emphasis over territorial disputes, actual war, siege battles and all the medieval shenanigans involved therein, so it's probably safe to say the game is named based on all that. 
Oh also the actual desert is called the "Crimson" desert in the video game. That too.

When I heard that some people thought weapon crafting was a bad thing I lost my mind.

The ability to get just one copy of a gun, and update it I overtime, so that I don't have like 5-20 copies of a gun just to have access to the different possible rolls? That was the best shit I ever heard about being added to Destiny.

Get a weapon once and you have it. All you have to do is level it up and you could get all of the possible rolls and you didn't need to keep farming that same gun over and over.

The rng roll guns in Destiny never felt like they mattered. If I got a copy with a roll that I wasn't looking for then I got a dud reward. If I got a copy that I was interested in trying but not the exact roll I'm looking for, I got vault fodder. And then if I finally get the roll I wanted I end up getting a bunch more copies that are duds because I might not be done playing that activity yet so even though I got the roll I wanted, I still have to deal with dud rolls cluttering my inventory/vault.

But with the crafted weapon system meant I just needed to farm a weapon once and I could customize it to be exactly what I want, and I can change it over time as my interests/needs change.

I think a good solution to cheaters is rather than ban them, warden them off into their own cheater space (WITHOUT INFORMING THEM).
Obviously this isn’t a perfect solution, and potentially really bad for false positives. The problem is, anyone willing to jump through the hoops to cheat in the first place is someone who’s willing to buy multiple accounts. If these people are unaware that they are in cheater jail, they can’t quickly boot up a new account to start over.

Upsides:
-keeps legit player economy much healthier
-slows the spread of cheating accounts
-gives the potential to mark players associated with cheating accounts and boosters before they are aware of their cheater status
-makes the game far worse for those who cheat or engage in boosting

Downside:
-False positives could lead to players being stuck in cheater hell forever and not know it
-Not necessarily a fool proof solution if tactics are developed to identify that you have been designated a cheater
-doesn’t actually completely prevent cheaters in the legit player economy (this is unavoidable as cheating is an endless arms race between game devs and cheat devs)
-bungie will gets less sales from account boosters (this in a just world shouldn’t be a problem, but the incentives for Sony/Bungie to see losing those sales as a potentially financially risk are a thing)

I am a stern advocate for basically never calling a game "dead" or "dying." While Bungie has a plethora of issues, both in-house and in-game, their games always tend to survive.

BUT...I will say this:

Bungie has 3 major fires they need to put out for Marathon or I fear Sony may step in and do something drastic to Bungie itself soon:

1) Faction progression has been a pretty obvious sore point for most or many players, especially in regards to some "basic" shell upgrades, and the community has been making that known lately as a very large, current detriment to the game atm.

2) The "battle royale" (or "wipe-everyone-in-the-lobby") meta, enabled by the sniper\shotgun\bubble meta and dominated by high-level players with nothing better to do, is absolutely crushing the fodder players' hopes of feeling like they can actually play the game, and it's causing many to straight-up quit (as seen by the decaying player count).

3) Cheaters.

#1 is fairly easy to put out imo, just needs some time, and changes for that may already be coming out as early as next week's patch.
#2 is much harder to put out. I'm not even sure what you can do to give the hardcores\grinders\streamers something to do in end game that doesn't end in them racking all the players up in every match. This may take a few months, or even a year, of change to douse that fire.
#3 is honestly a fire I don't believe is possible for them to put out at this point, and **that is absolutely frightening.** It's obvious BattleEye isn't working and hasn't worked over the past decade. But unless Bungie can find another reliable anti-cheat and pay for its use (doubt it) like Vanguard, which I believe also hardware bans, I would think their best hope is their own in-house anti-cheat. And since it's not only something they don't currently have, the fact they didn't even ALLUDE to the idea they may be making one means this game's life will literally hinge on if they can somehow nix JUST enough cheaters over time, on a consistent basis, to keep the game playable.

I still don't think Marathon is dead. And I still don't even think IT WILL die, unless Sony actually fully pulls the cord for purely financial reasons (also doubt it). There's a hardcore subset of people who love this game and, like D2, will continue to play it until it's literally taken offline.

With that being said, Bungie is absolutely *over the coals* and will continue to be until *ALL* 3 of these issues are doused.

Gonna be a **real** interesting future over the next 6 months.
